sources.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
sources.read_locator: Complete 39-page source document retrieved. Read §§2.2.2–2.2.3 (PDF pp. 15–18), §§2.3.1–2.3.3 (pp. 19–23), and §2.6.2 (pp. 28–30).
sources.source_kind_detail: Full author lecture-note PDF for the 2008 nonlinear conservation-law summer school; not an abstract or excerpt.
sources.extent: Inspected the full-text PDF and the complete monotone-scheme, BV/time-estimate, discrete-entropy, convergence and no-BV discussion sections used for this authoring. Other sections are not used as mathematical support.

contents.name: Monotone two-point flux, invariant interval and full CFL bound
contents.detail: The source defines consistency and coordinate monotonicity on the data interval, derives the sum-of-coordinate-Lipschitz CFL bound and identifies Godunov and modified Lax–Friedrichs examples. Batch 29 states its own full invariant-interval version and proves both example interfaces locally.

contents.name: Spatial TVD and discrete time-increment estimates
contents.detail: Propositions 2.3.1 and 2.3.3 support the range, TVD and temporal-translation route. The complete coordinate-Lipschitz and summability arguments are supplied in the local item.

contents.name: Crandall–Majda discrete Kruzhkov inequality
contents.detail: Proposition 2.3.6 uses the same maximum/minimum entropy flux and monotone update comparison; the local proof checks the full CFL map and levels outside the invariant interval.

contents.name: Monotone finite-volume convergence theorem
contents.detail: Theorem 2.3.9 supports the compactness–entropy-limit–uniqueness route. Its proof cites Helly compactness; batch 29 supplies the missing rational-point local proof and strong initial trace.

contents.name: No-BV entropy-process convergence route
contents.detail: Section 2.6.2 uses Young measures and a weak-BV estimate to treat data without BV. The approved claim remains scalar BV and does not import or extend that route.

sources.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik Skre Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws and Related Equations, ETH lecture notes
sources.read_locator: Complete 125-page lecture-note PDF retrieved. Read §4.4.4 (PDF pp. 49–50), §§4.5.2–4.5.4 (pp. 51–54), and §4.6 (pp. 55–57), including the full proof of Theorem 4.19.
sources.source_kind_detail: Full ETH Zürich course text authored by Mishra, Fjordholm and Abgrall; the complete PDF and text extraction are available locally.
sources.extent: Inspected the complete cited sections on Godunov/Lax–Friedrichs monotonicity, Crandall–Majda entropy flux, TVD/time continuity, Helly compactness and Theorem 4.19. Other chapters are not used as proof support.

contents.name: Godunov and Lax–Friedrichs monotonicity under CFL
contents.detail: Section 4.4.4 gives the Godunov monotonicity argument and Lax–Friedrichs derivative conditions; the local examples specialize and verify the full invariant-interval CFL interface.

contents.name: Discrete entropy flux and monotone update proof
contents.detail: Proposition 4.10 derives the max/min entropy flux using isotonicity of the three-point update. The local proof expands both invariant-interval and exterior entropy-level cases.

contents.name: TVD and temporal translation estimates
contents.detail: Lemmas 4.13–4.14 give the stability route used locally; the local proofs do not rely on the source’s unproved Helly extraction.

contents.name: Helly compactness and Theorem 4.19
contents.detail: Theorem 4.19 fixes the piecewise-linear time interpolant and the positive lower Δt/Δx premise. Theorem 4.18 is an L1 BV compactness statement; the complete local rational-point extraction and initial trace are proved in this batch.

contents.name: Global tail estimate in the source’s L1(R) convergence proof
contents.detail: The source uses U0∈L1(R), a global L1 bound and a finite-propagation tail estimate to obtain global L1 convergence. Batch 29 claims only local convergence and separately proves existence for nonintegrable bounded BV data.

contents.name: Lax–Friedrichs flux and its monotone CFL interface

contents.name: Burgers stationary shock example
contents.detail: The aligned compressive 1-to−1 stationary shock is recalculated exactly; the local proof also verifies all Kruzhkov levels.

contents.name: A nonmonotone flux with an exact expansion-shock limit
contents.detail: This polynomial counterexample is constructed and checked locally; no source example is imported as a supplier.
